data.narrative:
Mesh Optical Technologies is a Series A semiconductor company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors, with particular focus on same-stage companies including Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B).

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yields $100M. Peer-median triangulation across the 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produced a median of $2.0B, with observed range of $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple could not be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, which is typical for private companies.

The two applicable methods produce a triangulated range of $85M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects substantive tension between stage-based progression, which accounts for early-stage risk and modest capital deployed, and peer valuation, which reflects sector heat and significant late-stage private funding. Key uncertainties include traction metrics (customer adoption, technical milestones) and capital efficiency relative to named peers. Resolution of these factors will materially narrow the range before next fundraise.
